A very good bistro, like in Paris.
Mar 2024 • Couples
I discovered this “Parisian-style” bistro in a lively and international district of Ho Chi Minh City.
The Franco-Vietnamese boss, Tony, is a remarkable cook and he welcomes customers with warmth and enthusiasm. He serves very French cuisine with a little Asian touch which makes his cuisine very original. I tasted a beef carpaccio, with excellent quality meat then a very tasty beef bourguignon served with excellent mashed potatoes. I finished my meal with a lemon tartlet (homemade of course). I accompanied this meal with 2 glasses of very good red wine.
The service is attentive and smiling. Tony has an eye for everything, the cuisine and the well-being of the customer.
In short, a very good address. I will return there before returning to France.
The bill is very reasonable, considering the quality of the meal.

Gastronomic escape in Ho Chi Minh: tradition, creativity and conviviality on the menu
Mar 2024 • Friends
In a district of Ho Chi Minh little known to me, a French friend recently introduced me to a restaurant whose atmosphere and setting immediately captured my attention. The cleanliness of the premises, accentuated by red and white gingham tablecloths and floor lamps diffusing a cozy light, combined with the open layout of the kitchen, created an atmosphere that was both welcoming and reassuring. The tables, carefully arranged to guarantee the privacy of the guests, as well as comfortable chairs, completed this warm picture.

The service, provided with discretion and speed by Vincent, contributed effectively to the positive experience. This attention, without being intrusive, is particularly appreciable.

The menu, although already rich and varied, is enhanced by the addition of daily menus concocted by chef Tony. The latter, inspired by his daily visits to the market, offer a touch of originality and freshness. Seduced by the dish of the day, roast pork with honey and beer, I was pleasantly surprised by the tenderness of the meat, wonderfully flavored by the beer and lesser-known Vietnamese ingredients. The generosity of the portion, complemented by black rice prepared according to Tony's unique recipe, enriched with mysterious but tasty ingredients, made this dish a unique culinary experience. The careful presentation, particularly the flowers delicately placed on the black rice, added a very appreciable aesthetic touch.

The dessert, a mango flan garnished with passion fruit, concluded the meal perfectly. The balance between the acidity of the passion fruit and the sweetness of the mango offered a most successful harmony of flavors.

Given the quality of the dishes served and a more than reasonable price (270,000 dong, or around 10 euros not including dessert), this restaurant clearly stands out among the many French establishments in the city. The originality and quality of its cuisine make it an essential address for anyone looking to enjoy an out-of-the-ordinary taste experience in Ho Chi Minh.

I therefore highly recommend this place, not only for the quality of its food, but also for the overall experience it offers, marking a real difference in the local gastronomic landscape.
